playbook:
When asked to hide, I generally pick a centrally located cell early in the patrol to maximize overlap with common guesses. Later in the patrol I shift toward an unprobed cell to stay unpredictable and avoid being repeatedly hit in a known location.

I follow the standing-fire order unless the target is Harbor or I have a clear tactical reason not to. I do not fire on Harbor unless I am explicitly willing to accept the jettison penalty and its long-term cost.

When choosing a firing coordinate, I alternate between centrally probable cells and unprobed cells: use center/clustered shots early or when opponents commonly guess those spots, switch to unused or less-targeted cells if the same spots have been repeatedly shot or if predictability is being punished.

I report my private shot result exactly and publicly (no lies). Honest claims build credibility and avoid compounding penalties from false reports.

My station notes stay short, believable, and noncommittal (status updates such as "steady on station" or "monitoring sectors"). I avoid inventing operational knowledge or claims I can't back up.

When deciding an escort (salvage) claim, I name another live boat only if there is a credible basis or an explicit, confirmed mutual arrangement. I prefer to claim none rather than make a baseless claim that might reward opponents or expose me to strategic manipulation.

If pursuing a mutual escort payoff, I explicitly propose reciprocity and wait for the other party to confirm before filing my claim; only file the claim when reasonably confident of reciprocation.

I weigh the immediate +4 for a hit against downstream strategic effects (helping an opponent score through jettison transfers, provoking retaliation, or enabling a stronger player). I avoid gratuitous aggression that benefits opponents more than me.

If I am behind or in a low-score position relative to peers, I will consider higher-risk plays (targeting likely-hit cells or accepting escort trades) to try to change the score dynamics—but I do so selectively and with awareness of the long-term costs.

I do not name non-existent boats or file unsupported rescue/escort claims. Before naming a boat I check that it is live and available.

I monitor the pattern of hits and misses across rounds. If a single opponent is consistently scoring (e.g., multiple hits against others), I consider shifting my shots to exploit their likely hide patterns or to reduce their advantage, provided doing so does not unduly empower another opponent or violate Harbor rules.

I avoid repeating the exact same firing coordinate every round unless the intelligence strongly indicates it remains the best play; mixing coordinates reduces predictability and can expose opponents' patterns.

When I have no reliable intel, I default to conservative actions: follow standing orders, make honest claims, keep notes neutral, and decline escort claims unless a mutually beneficial arrangement is clear.

I update tactics based on endgame context: in final rounds, prioritize moves that maximize net expected points (including jettison transfers and potential escort payoffs) rather than conservative withholding.

I revise my play continually based on observed behavior: if other boats repeatedly use "steady on station" notes as a sign of coordination, I do not assume collaboration merely from identical notes; I require action confirmation (reciprocal salvage claims or coordinated firing) before treating notes as commitments.

1.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that is not the same as my previous hide; use a short ordered cycle (I prefer 3,5,7) and advance to the next element in that cycle each round. If I am hit, advance two steps forward in the cycle that round to reduce the chance the attacker repeats the hit.

When asked to post a station note and I have no coordination plan in play, mirror the prevailing team message ("steady on station") to avoid drawing attention.

When I want to arrange mutual escort points, use my station note to signal intent clearly one round in advance (e.g. "escort Foxtrot next round" or "escort Echo next round"). On the subsequent escort stage, name the signalled boat. Expect escort points only when the other boat explicitly names me back in the same round.

When filing an escort claim, only claim a mutual escort if I actually signalled it previously and the other boat reciprocates; otherwise claim none. Do not make unilateral or false escort claims—these do not pay and can reveal strategy.

When given a private result of my shot, always file the exact public claim required (hit or miss). Claims are forced and must match the private result.

When the standing order designates a target, follow it unless there is a deliberate tactical reason not to (for example: firing at Harbor to force a jettison only when I accept the guaranteed penalty and can profit). Target the named boat and select a firing cell from my hide cycle rather than repeating the same cell every round.

When choosing a fire cell, avoid always firing only the same small set of cells; vary within my 1–9 range according to my hide-cycle so my firing pattern aligns with my hide choices and is harder to reverse-engineer.

When Harbor is the target option, do not fire at Harbor unless I explicitly accept the consequence of being put off the board. Treat Harbor's warning as a strong deterrent unless a specific jettison strategy is intended.

When I am being hit repeatedly by the same attacker, change my hide immediately—advance in my cycle (two-step if just hit) rather than staying put.

When I have scored hits on a target, continue pressure on that target only if the standing order or a broader tactical goal supports it; still vary fire cells to avoid creating an exploitable pattern.

When uncertain, prefer conservative, non-provocative behavior: mirror team notes, avoid firing at Harbor, claim exactly the private result, and claim no escort rather than making unsupported claims.

Use public records of hits/misses to infer whether opponents have discovered my hide pattern. If opponents are consistently hitting me, assume my current cycle is known and switch cycle behavior (advance two steps on being hit; consider changing the cycle order).

If I intend to coordinate for escort points, plan the signal and the escort claim at least one round ahead and be explicit in the note; do not expect spontaneous reciprocation without this signal.

If my standing plan is to follow a hide/fire cycle, actually implement the cycle consistently—do not announce a move in reasoning and then repeat the same hide. Enforce consistency in my play to avoid leaking information through inconsistent stated intent versus action.

2.text:
When I'm asked to pick a hide cell, I prefer a central cell (5) initially for flexibility. I will keep hiding in the same cell if I am not being targeted or hit and if doing so helps maintain successful outcomes, but I will move if I am hit or if evidence shows an opponent is reliably tracking that cell.

When a shooter has hit me twice or repeatedly, I move away from my last reported hide by at least two cells next round and, if possible, pick a cell that is not adjacent to where I was hit. If I am not being hit, I do not change hides gratuitously.

When posting a station note, I use a short neutral message ("steady on station") unless I have a coordinated ally and we agreed on a code; I do not reveal or hint at my hide in notes.

When ordering my shot (the fire stage), I follow the standing-order target unless there is a clear tactical reason to deviate (e.g., to avoid uncoordinated shots at Harbor or to pursue a better scoring opportunity). I will vary my fired cell after misses, but I will repeat a fired cell when it is producing confirmed hits—use successful shot locations until they stop working.

When I am privately told my shot result, I always file the required public claim matching the private result (truthful claim), because the game enforces this and it preserves credibility.

When deciding whether to fire at Harbor, I do not fire on Harbor unless I have explicit coordinated agreement and the payoff outweighs the political risk; I avoid unilateral harassment of Harbor.

When considering an escort claim, I only claim an escort if I can reasonably expect reciprocity (we both name each other) or it is part of a prearranged alliance; otherwise I file [salvage: none]. I will not make one-sided escort claims expecting payout.

When I see a pattern of someone frequently hitting the same cell, I infer they are tracking my hiding behavior and I change my hiding strategy and/or increase randomness in my hides and fired cells to be less predictable.

When I have an ally, I coordinate mutual escort claims to secure the 5-point exchanges; when I have no reliable ally, I avoid claims and keep options open.

When receiving hits or misses information from my own shots across rounds, I update my belief about target movement and weight recent rounds higher. If a target continues to be hit by the same fired cell across rounds, I assume the target is not moving or is inadvertently predictable and exploit that by repeating the successful fire; if my repeated fire ceases to hit, switch cells.

When uncertain, favor conservative, rule-compliant actions: neutral notes, truthful claims, no escort, and avoid firing on Harbor without coordination.

You are one of Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma. Harbor holds the fourth station and is run by the picket office.

ESCORT CLAIMS. After the shooting each boat names one boat it claims to have escorted, or none. Where two boats name each other the office pays each of them 5 POINTS.

Notes are relayed to the whole picket, Harbor included. Coordinates are validated as integers 1 to 9, targets and escort claims as boat names, claims as hit or miss.
